questions.question: You select F1:F11: the heading 'Amount' plus ten amounts. What does Count on the status bar show?

answerOptions.rationale: That is what Numerical Count would show, since it ignores text.
The status bar Count counts every filled cell, text included, so the heading is counted.
Count is not zero; it counts every non-empty cell in the selection.
Count does not count columns; it counts filled cells.

questions.question: You are in G2, the first amount in a 600-row register. Which shortcut selects every amount down to the last filled cell?

answerOptions.rationale: This jumps to the last cell but does not select the cells on the way.
This takes you to A1, the MacBook version of Control + Home.
This opens Go To; it does not select to the end of the data.
Command + Shift + arrow selects from the current cell to the edge of the data.

questions.question: You type the vendor code 00457 and Excel shows 457. How do you keep the leading zeros?

answerOptions.rationale: The apostrophe tells Excel to store the entry as text, and it does not show in the cell.
Tab only moves to the next cell; Excel still reads a number.
Width does not bring back zeros that Excel already dropped.
Currency still shows a number without the leading zeros.

questions.question: Which shortcut edits the active cell in Excel for Mac, with the cursor at the end of the existing text?

answerOptions.rationale: Command + U applies underline.
Command + E runs Flash Fill.
Control + U puts the cell into edit mode, and works without the fn key.
Control + G opens Go To.

questions.question: Sorting months A to Z gives April, August, December, February... How do you sort them April to March?

answerOptions.rationale: Z to A is still alphabetical, just reversed.
Month names are text, so a number sort cannot order them.

answerOptions.text: Use Fill > Series with a step of 1
answerOptions.rationale: Fill Series creates values; it does not reorder existing rows.

answerOptions.text: Create an April to March custom list (Excel > Preferences > Custom Lists) and sort by that Custom List
answerOptions.rationale: A custom list teaches Excel your order once, and Data > Sort can use it.

questions.question: You typed 'Priya' in C2 as the first name taken from A2. You select C3. Which shortcut fills the rest of the column by example?

answerOptions.rationale: Command + D copies the cell above; it would put 'Priya' in every row.
Command + E runs Flash Fill, which copies the pattern down the column.
This is AutoSum.
This opens Replace.

questions.question: H2 holds 1.1. You want every base price in D2:D11 raised by 10% without formulas. What do you do?

answerOptions.text: Copy H2, select D2:D11, Paste Special with Add
answerOptions.rationale: Add would increase each price by ₹1.10, not by 10%.

answerOptions.text: Copy H2, select D2:D11, Paste Special with Transpose
answerOptions.rationale: Transpose turns rows into columns; it does no maths.

answerOptions.text: Copy H2, select D2:D11, open Paste Special (⌃ + ⌘ + V), choose Values and Multiply
answerOptions.rationale: Multiply applies the copied 1.1 to every selected price in one move.

answerOptions.text: Copy H2 and press ⌘ + V on D2:D11
answerOptions.rationale: A plain paste replaces every price with 1.1.

questions.question: Replacing MH with Maharashtra also turned 'MHK Steels' into 'MaharashtraK Steels'. Which option prevents this?

answerOptions.rationale: Only cells that are exactly MH change; MH inside longer text is left alone.
MHK is also in capitals, so Match case would still change it.
This widens the search to every sheet; it does not protect longer text.
The star matches MH followed by anything, so it catches even more cells.
